title: Founding date of San Jacinto and its name board
summary: No record survives since the cornerstone was destroyed; Larry Bornstein got the name sign; the club predates World War I and had a junior division.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Well tell me, Rogers, do you know when the San Jacinto Club was started? Was it...

That's what I'm saying now. I don't have the record of it, you know what I mean? I said I should have... I should have took that at Cornerstone, because they had the founders of the club. Yeah. And they had all the names. Not all the members. No, they had the five members of the Cornerstone. Yeah.
You see, because when these people turned in building down, they don't care nothing about the Cornerstone or nothing. Oh, I see.

You think the destruction people just came in and smashed everything? Yeah. That's an awful shame. Wish I would have thought about something like that. I don't know. Yeah, you should have been hanging around.
I know Larry Bornstein got the name over the door.
You know, the big wooden name over the door to San Jacinto over the front of it. Larry got that. He was hanging up in his restaurant. Yeah, we had the Cal Don there too.
Look out there. From the Cal Don your car. That's good.
All the way across up there in black letters. Yeah, in San Jacinto.

Yeah. And I had one put downstairs and I fixed that little board on there. The Jackson Muehler fixed that up, you know what I mean? That one up at the top was made with the club. The letters was cut out and the spot was painted black. Then they had all the names, the San Jacinto club.
See, in the late 20s, that club was up because I used to go to rehearsal. Yeah. So San Jacinto probably was up before the 20s. Oh yeah, I'm sure it was.
Before World War I. It was pretty old. Yeah.
Before World War I. All my brothers used to belong. Yeah.
And you said your father. My father.
Yeah, I was a youngster then, you know what I mean? You were your first job. I'm 74 now, you know.
See, all these clubs had a junior division too, you see. Had kids in there. Oh really?
